title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
description:
You are given two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2` sorted in **non-decreasing order** and an integer `k`.

Define a pair `(u, v)` which consists of one element from the first array (`nums1[i]`) and one element from the second array (`nums2[j]`). Two pairs with different index tuples `(i, j)` are considered distinct even if they contain the same values.

Return the `k` pairs `(u1, v1), (u2, v2), ..., (uk, vk)` with the **smallest sums** `u + v`. If multiple valid sets of `k` pairs share the `k`-th smallest sum, or if pairs appear in any order, any valid answer is accepted. The judge validates that your returned list contains `k` valid distinct-index pairs achieving the `k` smallest possible sums (`true`).
constraints: nums1 and nums2 both are sorted in non-decreasing order.
hints: Notice that for each fixed index `i` in `nums1`, the sequence `(nums1[i], nums2[0]), (nums1[i], nums2[1]), ...` is already sorted by sum.
Seed a min-heap with `(nums1[i] + nums2[0], i, 0)` for `i` from `0` to `min(len(nums1), k) - 1`.
Pop the smallest-sum pair `(s, i, j)` k times; after popping `(i, j)`, push `(nums1[i] + nums2[j + 1], i, j + 1)` if `j + 1 < len(nums2)`.

examples.explanation: The first 3 pairs with smallest sums are [1, 2] (sum 3), [1, 4] (sum 5), and [1, 6] (sum 7).
Both index pairs (0, 0) and (1, 0) produce [1, 1] with sum 2, so [[1, 1], [1, 1]] is returned.
The smallest pair is [1, 1] (sum 2); the second pair can be either [1, 2] or [2, 1] (both sum 3).

inputs.name: k
inputs.description: Number of smallest-sum pairs to return
